description: Change a sequence's emails with AI in one request, like the Emails view in the sequence editor: the prompt says what to change, in any language ("make the background cream", "remove the header", "new structure for email 2"). Without emailIds the prompt decides which emails: every email, unless it names some. A look change (background, colors, fonts) is made identical across the emails it touches, down to each kind of block's style. "Make them all look like email 1" copies that email's style exactly without AI, keeping each email's words. For design variations of an email use generate_sequence_email_variations: such a prompt returns 400 here. An email written in HTML is edited as HTML and keeps its theme. A/B test steps, steps without an email and steps that send the same email as an earlier step are skipped and listed in skipped. Each email succeeds or fails on its own: emails[].status is changed, unchanged (summary says why) or failed; changed emails are saved (saved:true) unless dryRun is true. Saved changes apply to the next sends of an active sequence. Runs synchronously and can take up to a minute; one request edits up to 12 emails, so pass emailIds in batches for longer sequences. A 503 means the AI could not tell which emails the prompt means and nothing changed: retry or pass emailIds. An email saved elsewhere meanwhile comes back with saved:false and an error instead of being overwritten. If the call times out, read get_sequence before retrying: changes may already be saved. To set exact values instead of asking the AI, use update_sequence_nodes.
